tone: warm, pastoral, earnest, communal, joyful, and urgent
target_reader: religion-naive adults and older adolescents near grade 6
translation_identity: firmly dynamic-equivalence, NLT-like in readability but independent

sealed_unit.instruction: The completed human-edited wording of Philippians 2:1-11 is excluded from blind drafting. Preserve only the source-text discourse connection into verse 12.

governing_rules: The prose serves the reader; the apparatus serves accountability.
Translate meaning, logic, tone, discourse movement, and theological force rather than Greek surface form.
Use clear natural oral English; reorder, split, unpack, and clarify implied relationships when comprehension benefits.
Preserve the paragraph's movement from continuing obedience, through God's enabling work, to blameless communal witness and shared sacrificial joy.
Do not make salvation earned by human effort; preserve the relationship between the command in verse 12 and God's prior and active work in verse 13.
Do not turn disputed clauses into unsupported commentary; document consequential resolutions as risks or human questions.
No comparison translations, traditional benchmark wording, conversational drafts, or sealed human wording may enter blind drafting.
existing_decisions: Use Christ and Jesus Christ naturally according to the source reference.
Maintain the reader-first dynamic center established by the audited Philippians 1 benchmark without exposing its wording to blind workers.

units.title: God at work in an obedient and joyful community
known_issues: Verse 12 begins with a logical consequence from the Christ-pattern immediately preceding it; preserve the connection without exposing the approved wording of verses 5-11.
The address and commands are plural and communal. Do not erase the corporate dimension, but do not force an exclusively corporate interpretation.
Verse 12's 'work out your own salvation' describes carrying salvation into effect or living out its results, not earning salvation. Preserve the command's force without creating works-righteousness.
Verse 12's 'fear and trembling' conveys profound seriousness, humility, and reverence; avoid casualness, but do not make believers terrified that God may withdraw salvation.
Verse 13 repeats the work/energize word family and attributes both willing and acting to God's active work in or among the believers. Preserve both the inner desire and outward action.
The final phrase of verse 13 may mean for God's good pleasure or according to His gracious purpose. Do not silently flatten the referent without documenting the choice.
Verse 14's second noun can concern disputes, arguments, doubts, or contentious reasoning. Choose natural wording that fits the communal warning.
Verse 15 echoes scriptural language about a crooked and distorted generation and depicts believers as God's blameless children shining like heavenly lights in the world.
Verse 16's ἐπέχοντες may mean holding firmly to the word of life or holding it out to others. Preserve the best contextual sense and flag the consequential alternative.
Verse 16's day of Christ and Paul's running/labor imagery express his hope that his ministry will prove fruitful, not personal vanity.
Verse 17 uses sacrificial and drink-offering imagery for Paul's possible death alongside the believers' faith-filled service. Make the relationship intelligible without erasing the image.
Verses 17-18 repeat joy and shared rejoicing. Preserve the mutual and communal force rather than reducing it to private happiness.

verses.greek: Ὥστε ἀγαπητοί μου καθὼς πάντοτε ὑπηκούσατε μὴ ὡς ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ μου μόνον ἀλλὰ νῦν πολλῷ μᾶλλον ἐν τῇ ἀπουσίᾳ μου μετὰ φόβου καὶ τρόμου τὴν ἑαυτῶν σωτηρίαν κατεργάζεσθε
θεὸς γάρ ἐστιν ὁ ἐνεργῶν ἐν ὑμῖν καὶ τὸ θέλειν καὶ τὸ ἐνεργεῖν ὑπὲρ τῆς εὐδοκίας
Πάντα ποιεῖτε χωρὶς γογγυσμῶν καὶ διαλογισμῶν
ἵνα γένησθε ἄμεμπτοι καὶ ἀκέραιοι τέκνα θεοῦ ἄμωμα μέσον γενεᾶς σκολιᾶς καὶ διεστραμμένης ἐν οἷς φαίνεσθε ὡς φωστῆρες ἐν κόσμῳ
λόγον ζωῆς ἐπέχοντες εἰς καύχημα ἐμοὶ εἰς ἡμέραν Χριστοῦ ὅτι οὐκ εἰς κενὸν ἔδραμον οὐδὲ εἰς κενὸν ἐκοπίασα
ἀλλὰ εἰ καὶ σπένδομαι ἐπὶ τῇ θυσίᾳ καὶ λειτουργίᾳ τῆς πίστεως ὑμῶν χαίρω καὶ συγχαίρω πᾶσιν ὑμῖν
τὸ δὲ αὐτὸ καὶ ὑμεῖς χαίρετε καὶ συγχαίρετέ μοι
